chunks: From the Book of Sawm (fasting), from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: The people say that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fasted twenty-nine days more often than he fasted thirty. He said: They have lied. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast less than thirty days until he was taken, and the month of Ramadan has not diminished, since Allah created the heavens, from thirty days and a night.

key_terms.السَّمَاوَاتِ: the heavens, mentioned in relation to Allah's creation
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: sawm (fasting), the act of ritual fasting discussed in the report
key_terms.تِسْعَةً وَعِشْرِينَ: twenty-nine, the number of days being denied as the usual length here
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ: thirty, the stated full length of the month in this narration
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the fasting month under discussion

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم fast Ramadan as twenty-nine days more often than thirty?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام rejecting the claim that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم frequently fasted Ramadan as twenty-nine days. It states that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did not fast fewer than thirty days and that Ramadan has not been deficient from thirty days and a night since Allah created the heavens.
